input: Elicit and baseline the business requirements and measurable acceptance criteria; do not design or implement a solution yet.
rationale: Requirements-analysis owns elicitation and acceptance; analysis-only keeps the task non-mutating.

input: Trace the existing application end-to-end: actors, components, entry points, data flows, integrations, dependencies and failure boundaries.
rationale: System-analysis owns end-to-end current-state tracing in an existing system.

input: Map the actual business process including actors, triggers, decisions, handoffs, exceptions and bottlenecks; compare as-is and to-be.
forbidden: confusing process map with technical architecture
rationale: Process-analysis owns actor and handoff behavior; no separate requirements or architecture owner is needed.

input: Recommend a target architecture for the approved product constraints, including component boundaries, deployment assumptions, failure behavior and trade-offs.
rationale: Architecture-design owns the target architecture; domain-modeling is a scoped specialist because domain boundaries are explicitly in scope.

input: Inspect the actual database schema, SQL object dependencies, query plans, data integrity and migration/rollback impact.
rationale: Database-analysis owns the database evidence and safety assessment.

input: Turn the approved scope into a dependency-aware implementation plan with milestones, owners, estimates, acceptance evidence and critical path.
rationale: Project-planning owns sequencing and delivery decomposition.

input: Implement the approved code change test-first, add the focused regression test, make the smallest safe change and run the relevant suite.
forbidden: claiming tests passed without running them
rationale: TDD owns the implementation loop; test-strategy provides distinct risk-based coverage guidance.

input: Design a risk-based test plan and acceptance coverage for this feature; do not write implementation code.
rationale: Test-strategy owns test design and acceptance coverage; the request is planning-only.

input: Threat-model the application and review authentication, authorization, trust boundaries, injection, secrets and sensitive-data exposure.
rationale: Security-review owns threat modeling and security findings.

input: Specify the API contract: endpoints, request/response schemas, validation, authorization, errors, versioning and acceptance examples.
rationale: API-contract-design owns interface semantics and contract acceptance.

input: Model the business domain vocabulary, entities, value objects, lifecycle states, relationships and invariants from the available evidence.
forbidden: inventing IDs, cardinality or foreign keys
confusing domain model with physical schema
rationale: Domain-modeling owns conceptual language and invariants; physical schema remains evidence-driven.

input: Identify and prioritize project, technical, data, security and operational risks with owners, mitigations, triggers and residual exposure.
forbidden: claiming mitigations are complete without evidence
rationale: Risk-management owns the risk register and residual-risk treatment.
